transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
The president of Cornell University responded Saturday to charges by a student that she was gang-raped at a fraternity in 2024.
New York's governor said Friday the investigation into those charges was flawed.
President Michael Kotlikoff released a video statement saying the university must do better.
There are real legal and privacy limits on what we can say.
But we will make a greater effort to explain what we can, to provide context about the actions Cornell has taken, and to be more transparent.
The New York State Attorney General is now taking over the investigation.
There are new details into the investigation of the mid-air attack aboard a commercial plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.
As NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports, the United Arab Emirates has deemed the incident an attempted terrorist attack.
Investigators in the UAE announced that the Fly Dubai co-pilot who carried out the attack mid-flight assaulted the captain of the plane using what's called a crash axe,
a lightweight emergency tool stored in the cockpit to break through panels or jam doors in the event of a crash.
Investigators said the attacker then tried to seize control of the plane's flight mechanisms.
The plane had 174 people on board, many of whom are Israeli.
Israeli officials had already deemed it an attempted terrorist attack.
Emirati investigators have now agreed.
Both the pilot and co-pilot are live and being questioned, and the investigation is ongoing.
Israel has said the attacker is from Oman, although that has yet to be confirmed by Emirati, Saudi, or Omani officials.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Protests are continuing across Spain at this hour as residents demand the government take urgent action to address a national housing crisis.
NPR's Miguel Macias has our story.
Much has happened since the protests started a week ago after 87-year-old Maria Del Carmen Yavascal was evicted from her rental apartment in Madrid.
The government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez drafted two emergency housing decrees in a rush negotiating with the Scottish members.
While all parties in Spain agree there is a national problem with the price of rental housing, they did not agree on a solution.
On Friday, Sanchez's measures were voted down.
In Congress, there's been plenty of finger-pointing and speculation that Sanchez might call snap elections for late November,
as he sees an opportunity to come from behind in the polls thanks to an energized left.
On the streets, protesters continue to demand solutions now.
Miguel Macias, NPR News, Seville, Spain.
The head of Tennessee's prison system is resigning. Frank Strada says stepping aside is in the best interests of the state.
Corrections officials had tried to execute a prisoner on Wednesday, but the botched attempt left the prisoner unconscious in a hospital.
Governor Bill Lee announced the resignation on Saturday, calling the circumstances a difficult moment.
You're listening to NPR News.
Voters are heading to the polls in Brazil on Sunday to elect a new president.
Current President Luis Inazio Lula da Silva is looking for his fourth non-consecutive term.
He held a parade in downtown Sao Paulo Saturday, while challenger Flavio Bolsonaro traveled to cities further out in the state.
A new study shows that eating with another person may help you manage your blood sugar.
As NPR's Burley McCoy reports, researchers gave two groups of participants the same amount of bread to eat, then measured how their blood sugar rose and recovered.
In one group, the participants ate their bread alone.
In the other, someone else was in the room, and they found the social eaters recovered quicker.
That is, their blood sugar didn't spike as high or came back down quicker, or both.
Lead author and behavioral neuroscientist Shir Adziel says this might be because humans are social animals.
If my brain develops in a social context, my brain learns to regulate my glucose levels in social proximity.
She says other people may be a social cue the brain uses to start processing sugar earlier, for example by releasing insulin, which helps regulate blood sugar.
The results appear in the journal Science Advances, Burley McCoy and NPR News.
President Trump is lobbying senators to pass a measure that would make daylight savings time permanent.
He says doing so would provide more daylight during times when most Americans are active.
On Saturday, posted on social media, what he says is the personal cell phone number of Republican Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas, who has been a critic of that bill.
He is urging people to call Cotton and demand that he support the bill.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
